title.en: Those who stay awake so we can sleep

text.en: While you sleep tonight, someone is standing guard on a frozen mountain or in a burning desert. This poem by Dr A.P.J. Abdul Kalam is a thank-you to them. Here we study it in our own words, and you can read the original in your textbook.

You look around and identify people who contribute to your life selflessly, even at risk to their own lives, and in pairs you prepare three questions you would like to ask them.
A.P.J. Abdul Kalam, India's eleventh President and a missile scientist, wrote this poem as a tribute to the Indian soldiers. A note in the book explains that when the poet says great sons, he means all soldiers, men and women, who serve the nation.
The poet addresses the defenders of the borders and calls them great sons of the motherland. While the rest of us sleep, they keep doing their duty. Whether it is windy, snowy or scorching hot, they stay awake and on guard. They tread lonely stretches of land, calm and patient like yogis. Their duty takes them to mountain heights, valleys, deserts and marshes. They keep watch over the seas and secure the skies. They have given the prime of their youth, the best years of life, to the nation. The poet says the wind chimes of the land carry the sound of their deeds, then ends by praying for the brave men and asking God to bless them all.
The theme is patriotism and sacrifice. The tone is grateful, respectful and prayerful. Imagery appears in windy season, snowy days and scorching sun, which let us picture the hardships. Yogis is a comparison: soldiers are likened to yogis for their calm, disciplined, lonely dedication. The wind chimes are a metaphor for the land itself honouring the soldiers. Repetition of you and we sets the soldiers against the sleeping citizens and shows our gratitude. Alliteration in phrases such as season and snowy adds music.
Terrains are physical features of land, such as valleys, deserts, marshes, plateaus and plains. The poem names valleys, deserts and marshes. Collocations are word pairs that commonly go together, such as scorching sun. In the exercise, the natural pairs are summit of the mountain, barren landscape, dense forest, adventurous person and not making any promises. We make promises, not do them.
In Let us listen you complete a short poem called A Soldier's Pride by listening, then check your answers against the recording. The blanks follow a rhyme pattern, so the missing words rhyme with their neighbouring lines. In Let us speak you recite the poem in pairs and groups, pausing at the marked breaks, using volume to show emotion, keeping a steady pace, using facial expressions and standing tall. In Let us write you compose an acrostic poem, where the first letters of the lines spell a word such as SOLDIER, and draft a gratitude note of about 50 words beginning Dear Bravehearts. In Let us explore you design a badge of honour with a logo and slogan, and find a poem or story in your mother tongue about soldiers' bravery to present in class.
The speaker is a citizen of the country, shown by phrases such as my land and we pray. Opposites in the extract include asleep and awake, and windy and snowy against scorching. Still hold on to your deed shows their attitude of dedication to duty, and the quality highlighted is dedication. Praying for soldiers matters because it shows gratitude and reminds us that our peaceful lives depend on their sacrifice.

problem.en: Match the device to the reason it is used in the poem.

text.en: Simile or metaphor for yogis and wind chimes.

why.en: They show the calm dedication of soldiers and the land honouring them.

text.en: Repetition of you and we.

why.en: It contrasts the soldiers on guard with the sleeping citizens.

problem.en: Complete: Terrains in the poem are valleys, deserts and ____.

text.en: Which wet land is named?
Which are not terrains named?

why.en: Oceans and sky are not terrains here.

prompt.en: Write a short appreciation of the poem My Dear Soldiers.

requiredIdeas.en: It is a tribute to soldiers by A.P.J. Abdul Kalam.
It shows them guarding in all weather and terrain.
It uses imagery, repetition and metaphor.
It ends with prayers for their well-being.

points.en: The poem by A.P.J. Abdul Kalam is a tribute to soldiers who guard the nation day and night.
Soldiers face winds, snow and heat, and guard mountains, valleys, deserts, marshes, seas and air.
The theme is patriotism and sacrifice and the tone is grateful and prayerful.
Collocations are word pairs that naturally go together.
We should respect soldiers and pray for them.
